name: Sallai
overview: Sallai was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. His presence is noted in the post-exilic period, reflecting the resettlement of the city. Sallai's identification as a Benjaminite highlights his tribal heritage within Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Sallai possibly means 'God had restored,' indicating a connection to divine restoration. This meaning aligns with the context of the return to Jerusalem after exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:8.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Sallai as a descendant of Benjamin. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Sallai's significance lies in his representation of the Benjaminite families who resettled Jerusalem following the Babylonian exile. His mention underscores the fulfillment of God's promise to restore His people to their land. As a resident of Jerusalem, Sallai contributes to the biblical narrative of the community's renewal under God's providence.
